identity.description: Closed-form Bayes classifier under the strong assumption that features are conditionally INDEPENDENT given the class. Fits in one pass (per-class moments or counts), works at tiny n, ranks well — and is famously miscalibrated when features correlate, because shared evidence gets multiplied in as if it were new.

consumes.note: variant-split contract: continuous features → GaussianNB; non-negative count-like features → MultinomialNB (negative values are a hard error there)

emits.note: famously MISCALIBRATED: the independence violation multiplies correlated evidence repeatedly, piling posteriors onto 0/1 — ranking is usually decent, but these probabilities must pass through an external calibrator before any thresholded or expected-value use
argmax survives miscalibration better than the probabilities do

var_smoothing.note: GaussianNB only — additive variance floor (a fraction of the largest feature variance) against zero-variance collapse

alpha.note: MultinomialNB only — Laplace/Lidstone smoothing against zero-count features

fit_prior.note: MultinomialNB only — learn class priors from data vs uniform

priors.note: GaussianNB only — explicit class priors override; leave null

invariances.why: GaussianNB posteriors are invariant to per-feature affine rescaling — the Gaussian density's Jacobian factor is identical across classes and cancels in the posterior ratio; the caveat is MultinomialNB, where the absolute count magnitude IS the evidence weight and scaling corrupts it
a nonlinear monotone map (log, rank) changes the per-class feature distribution shape, and the Gaussian likelihood fits the actual values — the fit changes
the factorized likelihood could in principle skip missing terms, but sklearn's implementations reject NaN input
this driver ships Gaussian/Multinomial variants only — raw categoricals must be encoded (sklearn's CategoricalNB exists but is not wired here)

two stacked assumptions: conditional independence of features given the class (the 'naive' core), plus a per-feature Gaussian (or multinomial count) likelihood — both are load-bearing and both are commonly violated
parameters are closed-form per-class moments/counts — one O(n·p) pass, no optimization, sensible estimates from tens of rows, and streaming via partial_fit
the class-conditional Gaussians are defined on all of ℝ — far outside the training range the log-likelihood ratio grows quadratically, producing extremely (over)confident posteriors with no warning

featureStats.why: the independence assumption is violated in exact proportion to inter-feature correlation — correlated features get their shared evidence multiplied in repeatedly, the mechanism behind the 0/1 posterior pile-up
GaussianNB fits a symmetric Gaussian per feature per class; heavy skew misfits that likelihood and a symmetrizing transform directly repairs it
MultinomialNB: a feature never seen with a class zeroes the whole posterior product without smoothing — the direct justification for the alpha prior

modelMetrics.why: NB's trademark failure mode is good ranking with terrible calibration — a large AUC-vs-Brier disparity is the signature, and the signal to wire a calibrator downstream rather than discard the model
the fraction of predictions with max posterior > 0.99 measures the evidence-double-counting directly — it should track feature correlation, not true class separability

edgeCases.behavior: shared evidence counted multiple times — posteriors saturate at 0/1
edgeCases.note: calibrate downstream and/or decorrelate upstream; ranking often survives

edgeCases.behavior: hard ValueError — counts must be non-negative

edgeCases.note: var_smoothing absorbs it; note the feature

edgeCases.condition: class absent or near-absent in training
edgeCases.behavior: prior ≈ 0 makes the class unreachable at predict time

edgeCases.condition: predict-time values far outside the training range
edgeCases.behavior: quadratically growing log-likelihood ratio — meaningless extreme confidence

driver.constructor: GaussianNB(**hp) or MultinomialNB(**hp) — variant selected by the input feature profile (continuous → Gaussian; non-negative counts → Multinomial)
driver.wrapperNeeds: variant selection from the input profile; route the probability port through an external calibrator by default

canBeSeeds.note: NB + external calibration is the canonical pairing — it keeps the ranking and repairs the trademark miscalibration

placementClaims.why: sklearn's NB implementations reject NaN — rows must be imputed upstream
symmetrizing skewed features improves the per-feature Gaussian likelihood fit that GaussianNB assumes
GaussianNB is affine-invariant per feature (standardization is wasted compute), and for MultinomialNB standardization produces negative values that hard-error — counts must arrive raw
no native categorical variant in this driver; categoricals must be encoded before the likelihood factorizes over them
